findings.title: traceID field dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' log line
findings.body: The previous implementation of logRequest explicitly appended "traceID" to the log parameters via tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false), and the tracing import was removed along with that code. The replacement relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx), which only picks up contextual attributes stored in the context via log.WithContextualAttributes — and the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware (instrumentContext) only sets endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, and uname; it never sets traceID. Nothing else in the middleware chain injects traceID as a contextual log attribute, so the traceID field that operators previously had for correlating these plugin request logs with traces silently disappears from the "Plugin Request Completed" log line whenever plugin_log_backend_requests is enabled. If traceID was intended to be kept, it should either be re-added explicitly to logParams or included in the contextual attributes by the ContextualLoggerMiddleware.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, discarding captured logs
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns NewTestLogger(), i.e. a fresh, empty TestLogger. Since LoggerMiddleware now logs through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...) instead of calling the injected logger directly, any test that passes a TestLogger and then asserts on its InfoLogs/WarnLogs fields will see zero calls — the log entry is recorded on the discarded instance, so the assertion fails (or, worse, if written to tolerate absence, silently passes). The fake should return the receiver itself (return f) so logs emitted through the FromContext path are captured on the same object the test holds.

findings.title: Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after rename
findings.body: The middleware was renamed from InstrumentationMiddleware to MetricsMiddleware and the test file was renamed accordingly, but the top-level test function is still called TestInstrumentationMiddleware. This is a leftover of the rename and makes test output/searching refer to a type that no longer exists; it should be renamed to TestMetricsMiddleware for consistency with the rest of the PR.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware still constructed with logger name 'plugin.instrumentation'
findings.body: CreateMiddlewares builds the LoggerMiddleware with log.New("plugin.instrumentation"). Since the InstrumentationMiddleware no longer exists (it is now MetricsMiddleware, plus a separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware), the 'plugin.instrumentation' logger name is a stale reference to the removed type and makes log source attribution misleading — log lines emitted by the LoggerMiddleware now appear to come from an 'instrumentation' component that was deliberately renamed. A name such as 'plugin.logger' or 'plugin.client' would reflect the new structure.
